Key design points: Firebase tokens are verified on every request with revocation checking; the daily quota is reserved in a transaction before any model is called; images are validated by file signature; the provider layer is an abstraction (\texttt{gemini}, OpenAI-compatible) with per-model capability checks; logs contain identifiers, counts and timings only.

Show the overlay first, capture behind it & Overlay on screen in 5--39 ms instead of waiting for the capture \\
Screen copy through GDI BitBlt in a native helper & Screenshot in 109--338 ms; Electron's built-in grabber took up to 2.8 s after the app had been idle \\
Compiled C\# helper instead of a PowerShell host & 16 MB instead of about 127 MB; ready in about 100--400 ms \\
Software rendering by default & About 100 MB less memory with no visible difference for this interface \\
OCR engine loaded on demand and unloaded after idle & No cost until a capture is started \\

\section{Security}

The full control-by-control analysis, with the code location and the test that proves each control, is in \texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}SECURITY.\allowbreak{}md}. Summary:

{\small
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{\dimexpr(\textwidth-4\tabcolsep)*233/1000\relax}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{\dimexpr(\textwidth-4\tabcolsep)*767/1000\relax}}
\caption{Security}\\
\toprule
\rowcolor{tblhead}\textbf{Area} & \textbf{Controls} \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
\rowcolor{tblhead}\textbf{Area} & \textbf{Controls} \\
\midrule
\endhead
\bottomrule
\endfoot
\textbf{Authentication} & Firebase ID token required for every \texttt{/\allowbreak{}v1/\allowbreak{}*} call; signature and revocation verified; disabled and revoked users refused immediately \\
\textbf{Authorization} & Quota and usage keyed by the verified user id; Firestore rules deny all client access, including a user reading or resetting their own quota \\
\textbf{Secrets} & Gemini key and service account only in server secrets; none in the repository or the client; no key file at all on Cloud Run; user keys encrypted with Windows DPAPI \\
\textbf{Input validation} & Size, count and length limits; images checked by file signature (a fake PNG is rejected); a model that cannot read images never receives one \\
\textbf{Abuse and cost control} & Per-IP and per-user rate limits; daily quota in an atomic transaction; upstream timeout; upstream cancelled when the client disconnects \\
\textbf{Transport and platform} & HTTPS only (the client refuses non-HTTPS backends except localhost); \texttt{helmet} security headers; non-root container; 0 known vulnerabilities in production dependencies, enforced in CI \\
\textbf{Privacy} & Nothing stored or logged: no screenshots, OCR text, prompts or tokens; users are told what will be sent; a blur tool and local-only mode \\
\textbf{Client hardening} & Sandboxed renderers, context isolation, strict content-security policy, tokens never reach the UI \\
\textbf{Safe development mode} & The authentication bypass used for local work is refused in production or on a public interface \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
}

A STRIDE threat model and an honest list of remaining limitations (per-instance minute limiter, no App Check, no email verification, unsigned installer) are in \texttt{docs/\allowbreak{}SECURITY.\allowbreak{}md}.
